title: Recent advances in generalized thermoelasticity theory and the modified models: a review
authors: Farshad Shakeriaski; Maryam Ghodrat; Juan Escobedo-Diaz; Masud Behnia
unified_law: The review presents a combined governing formulation with relaxation-time terms spanning classical, Lord-Shulman, Green-Lindsay, Green-Naghdi, dual-phase-lag, and multi-phase-lag cases; parameter choices recover model variants.
geometries_covered: Reviewed applications include isotropic layers and strips, rotating disks, spherical sheets and cavities, hollow cylinders, beams, cracks, half-spaces, and three-dimensional bodies; these are separate cited studies.
experimental_evidence: The abstract says generalized theories are motivated by second-sound experiments; the review itself reports no new experiment or direct experimental test of its combined formulation.
limitations: The conclusion says higher-order time derivatives can weaken wave propagation and phase-lag choices influence wave viscosity; it says MPL and GN-I combine attenuation and dispersion whereas DPL does not.

title: A critical review of non-Fourier heat transfer theories with phase lag in bio-heating: Explaining the variations in reported phase lag coefficients
authors: Mohammad Azhdari; Ghader Rezazadeh; Raghav Pathak; Hans-Michael Tautenhahn; Franziska Tautenhahn; Tim Ricken; Seyed Morteza Seyedpour
unified_law: The paper compares CV/SPL, DPL, and TPL laws rather than deriving one unified law: one, two, and three lag terms, with stated limits returning simpler models.
geometries_covered: The review focuses on bioheating in biological tissue; discussed experiments use processed-meat cylinders, porous or granular samples, layered tissue phantoms, and bovine-skin disks.
experimental_evidence: The review summarizes prior experiments, not a new experiment: processed meat showed finite-speed wave interactions; a cited Roetzel study reported a small but measurable effect in porous media; a cited bovine-skin study reported small phase-lag values.
limitations: The abstract and conclusion report phase lags near zero to 32 s, while Section 3 also cites values as high as 500-600 (the synthesis sentence does not repeat the unit); the authors say many values lack clear rationale and rigorous independent validation is limited.

title: On The Phase- Lag Green-Naghdi Thermoelasticity Theories
authors: Ahmed S. El-Karamany; Magdy A. Ezzat
unified_law: The article sets out one heat-flux law and transport equation with selectable lag parameters; it states that SPL-GN-III, DPL-GN-II, DPL-GN-III, Cattaneo, Lord-Shulman, GN-II, coupled, and Fourier cases follow as reductions.
thermodynamic_restrictions: The paper adopts xi=0 for GN-II and analyzes T*xi>0 for other cases under positive-definite conductivity tensors and positive material quantities; it separately notes a second-law objection to Lord-Shulman theory.
geometries_covered: The general problem is a linear anisotropic inhomogeneous solid on a regular 3D region with piecewise-smooth boundary; the example is a 1D isotropic homogeneous traction-free half-space under a surface thermal shock.
limitations: The formulation assumes linear small-field response; selected lag laws are Taylor-expanded to first order. The plotted application is a copper-like 1D isotropic half-space, and no experiment is reported. The paper also flags a second-law objection to Lord-Shulman theory.
evidence_page: printed page unnumbered (accepted-manuscript cover); PDF page index 1; printed pp.2-27; PDF page indices 3-28

title: On a multi-phase-lag model of coupled thermoelasticity
unified_law: The refined law tracks phase lags of heat flux, temperature gradient, and thermal-displacement gradient; the paper derives reductions including DPL, Lord-Shulman, GN-II/III, classical, and Green-Lindsay cases.
geometries_covered: General equations are stated for anisotropic thermoelastic solids; the worked photothermal example is an isotropic semiconducting beam with length, width, and thickness coordinates and L/h=10.
benchmarks: The paper calls its beam calculation a validation example and compares RPL, classical, Lord-Shulman, and GN predictions; no external benchmark dataset or measured reference is identified.
limitations: The evidence is a plot-based comparison for one photothermal semiconducting beam; no measured experimental validation is supplied. The refined model uses truncated time-lag expansions and a selected lag order.

title: Heat waves
unified_law: The review treats heat flux as a relaxation-kernel-weighted history of the temperature gradient; Cattaneo and Jeffreys forms are related choices, and fast/slow modes yield effective conductivity and capacity.
geometries_covered: Canonical cases are plane harmonic waves, weak singularities, and strong singularities posed in a semi-infinite region with boundary data at x=0; the review also treats dielectric-crystal second sound.
experimental_evidence: The review reports observed second sound in helium II and low-temperature dielectric crystals; it cautions that crystal oscillation response was unclear and successful experiments used pulses with incompletely known harmonic content.
limitations: The authors say one exponential relaxation time is unlikely to describe real conductors, effective conductivity can restore diffusion-like immediate response, internal-energy memory is little known, and ordinary-material wave speeds are difficult to measure.
